tagline: A loop through rice and crawfish country.
intro: The byway makes a 55-mile loop out of Jennings through Welsh and Lake Arthur, on the southwest Louisiana prairie, past rice fields and crawfish ponds. More than 160 kinds of birds turn up along it, and each fall a festival is held for the rice and the yellow rail, a rare and elusive marsh bird that winters on the Gulf Coast.
On the way lies Lacassine National Wildlife Refuge, set aside in 1937 for migratory birds, nearly 35,000 acres and most of it freshwater marsh and open water.

moments.title: Jennings
moments.text: Sylvester Cary came down from Iowa in 1883 seeking a home with neither winter nor mortgages, and wrote to his Iowa friends until they came too, settlers the locals called Yankees.

moments.title: Welsh
moments.text: Henry Welsh's cabin and store sat on the main stagecoach route across south Louisiana, the chief stop between New Iberia and Texas, and in 1880 he gave the railroad its right-of-way.

moments.title: Lake Arthur
moments.text: Travelers passing an early Acadian settler named Arthur LeBlanc took to calling the water le lac d'Arthur, and the name held for the lake and for the town with its park and boardwalk.
